headline: RBI: UNSC ISIL & Al-Qaida Sanctions List amended for 81 entries; REs to comply under UAPA s.51A
summary_points: RBI circular conveys UNSC Committee's amendment of 81 entries on the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions List, per UNSC press release SC/16516 dated November 20, 2026.
Amendments follow the 2025 Annual Review under paragraphs 92-95 of UNSC resolution 2734 (2024); measures are assets freeze, travel ban and arms embargo.
Regulated entities must act under Chapter IX of the RBI KYC Directions, 2025 and follow the UAPA Order of February 2, 2021 (amended April 22, 2024).
De-listing requests received by a bank are to be forwarded electronically to Joint Secretary (CTCR), MHA; applicants may also approach the UN Ombudsperson.
who_is_affected: Banks, small finance and payment banks, co-operative banks, RRBs, LABs, NBFCs, ARCs and AIFIs, particularly their KYC/AML and compliance teams.
action_required: Update sanctions screening against the amended UNSC entries, ensure no accounts are held in listed names, and follow the UAPA Order procedure for any match.

social.linkedin:
RBI has issued a circular (RBI/2026-27/308) on implementing Section 51A of the UAPA, 1967, following amendments to the UNSC's ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions List.

Key points:
- The UNSC Committee amended 81 entries (press release SC/16516, November 20, 2026) after the 2025 Annual Review.
- The sanctions comprise an assets freeze, travel ban and arms embargo.
- Regulated entities, including banks, NBFCs and ARCs, must act under Chapter IX of the RBI KYC Directions, 2025 and follow the UAPA Order dated February 2, 2021 (amended April 22, 2024).
- De-listing requests received by a bank must be forwarded electronically to Joint Secretary (CTCR), MHA.

Compliance teams should refresh their screening databases and confirm that no accounts exist in the names of listed persons or entities.

Please verify the details with the official RBI circular and the UN sanctions list before acting.
